Broxbourne's population increased by around 5,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 99,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Broxbourne increased by 5.8%, from around 93,600 in 2011 to around 99,000 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Broxbourne was home to around 13.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 13.0 in 2011. This area was among the top 35% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Broxbourne than across the East of England

Median age in Broxbourne

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Broxbourne increased by one year, from 39 to 40 years of age.

This area had a slightly lower average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but had a similar averaage (median) age to England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 2,800 (an increase of 17.2%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 700 (3.4% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Broxbourne residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 80,300 Broxbourne residents said they were born in England. This represented 81.1% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 81,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 86.8% of Broxbourne's population.

Turkey was the next most represented, with just over 2,000 Broxbourne residents reporting this country of birth (2.0%). This figure was up from just under 800 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.8% of the population of Broxbourne.

The number of Broxbourne residents born in countries that joined the EU between April 2001 and March 2011 (other than Poland, Croatia, Lithuania and Romania) rose from around 950 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to just over 1,800 in 2021 (1.8%).

In 2021, 81.1% of Broxbourne residents reported their country of birth as England

Ethnic groups in Broxbourne

In 2021, 4.6% of Broxbourne residents identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group"), up from 0.8% in 2011. The 3.7 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from the "Other ethnic groups" ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.5% to 1.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 1.0% to 2.2%.

In 2021, 81.1% of people in Broxbourne identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.3% in 2011), while 6.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 4.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 2.3% in 2011 to 4.0% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 4.6% of usual residents in Broxbourne identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group")

More lone parents

Broxbourne saw the East of England's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of lone-parent households (from 11.8% in 2011 to 13.7% in 2021).

Across the region, only Thurrock saw a greater rise in the percentage of lone-parent households (from 11.2% to 13.5%).

The percentage of households including a lone parent in Broxbourne increased by 1.9 percentage points

Fall in home ownership

Broxbourne saw the East of England's third-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of households that owned their home (from 72.9% in 2011 to 68.6% in 2021).

Across the region, only Watford (from 61.6% to 55.1%) and Luton (from 60.2% to 53.9%) saw a greater decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home.

Every local authority area across the East of England saw a fall in the percentage of households that owned their home, as the regional percentage fell from 67.6% to 65.2%.

The rate of home ownership in Broxbourne decreased by 4.3 percentage points

Health in Broxbourne

In 2021, 48.7% of Broxbourne residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.1% to 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Broxbourne residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.0% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.0% to 3.5%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Broxbourne increased by 3.4 percentage points

National identity in Broxbourne

In 2021, 9.9% of Broxbourne residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 7.6% in 2011.

In 2021, around 1 in 50 people (2.0%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.1% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Broxbourne that identified as "British only" increased from 15.5% to 55.1%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in Broxbourne (2.3 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Broxbourne increased by 2.3 percentage points

Unpaid care in Broxbourne

In 2021, 4.2% of Broxbourne residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 6.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The proportion of Broxbourne residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care decreased from 2.6% to 2.5%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Broxbourne (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Broxbourne decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Religion in Broxbourne

In 2021, 33.0% of Broxbourne residents reported having "No religion", up from 23.8% in 2011. The rise of 9.2 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Broxbourne. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 53.0% of people in Broxbourne described themselves as Christian (down from 65.0%), while 5.9% did not state their religion (down from 7.0% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 33.0% of usual residents in Broxbourne reported having "No religion"

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Broxbourne residents aged 16 years and over, 37.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 32.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (45.4%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 49.0% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Broxbourne that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.8% to 9.0%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Broxbourne (4.3 percentage points) than across the East of England (3.7 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Broxbourne increased by 4.3 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Broxbourne residents aged 16 years and over, 59.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 60.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.9%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.8% in 2011. The percentage of retired Broxbourne residents decreased from 21.0% to 20.4%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater across the East of England (1.1 percentage points, from 58.4% to 57.3%) than in Broxbourne (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Broxbourne decreased by 0.7 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 10.6% of Broxbourne residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.5% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Broxbourne (1.0 percentage points) than across the East of England (0.4 percentage points, from 10.4% to 10.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Broxbourne increased by 1.0 percentage points

Disability in Broxbourne

In 2021, 6.3% of Broxbourne residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 12 people (8.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.2% in 2011. The proportion of Broxbourne residents who were not disabled increased from 83.1% to 85.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Broxbourne (1.3 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Broxbourne decreased by 1.3 percentage points
